title: Reminiscing in Tempo and Duke always looking forward
summary: Duke wrote every day and never looked back; his biggest hits came from the original band when men chipped in.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: listen, let's -- I won't get off the track too much. Now, wait just a second. In about 1935 -- I guess it was '34, '35, that the band came to the Congress Hotel. Remember?
Yeah.
Followed Goodman. Remember?
Yeah.

Goodman -- that was -- Goodman was just -- well, that's '36. I guess it must be in '36, because Goodman had gone to the West Coast and just made it, and then they came to Chicago, and they were in the Congress, and they were a hit. And then Duke came in afterwards. And one of the things I remember about that was that he played "Reminiscing in Tempo". So evidently, that was his first extended work, "Reminiscing in Tempo", wasn't it? Do you remember?
No, I don't.

You don't. Well, that was the first time that he'd ever written anything that was out of tempo, you know, and, well I don't know how long that ran, but I guess it ran about 12 minutes, or something like that. That was the first thing, I think. Oh, you don't remember that. He didn't -- in later years, he didn't play that so much, did he?
No.
But you know, I think that that must have been the year his Mother died, Cootie, I think.
Yeah.
Because I believe that you know, that it was partly -- sprang from his, well, reminiscing, you see? I think he was going back, thinking back.
Well, I'll tell you about Duke. He never did go back. Not unless it was a special thing. He was always going forward. He was writing music every day and night. He never did think about going back.
Yeah.
He always was thinking about going forward.
Going forward. Yeah.
Yeah.

Well, I mean, he never was in a position where he had to wonder what he was going to think up next. There was a huge store of stuff there, wasn't there, for him to -- he just kept bringing it out, didn't he?
Yeah. He continuously was writing music, to write music, to write music, so he didn't have time to go back maybe ten years and bring up things, because he always had new things.

Yeah. And sometimes he would be coming up with a real beautiful melody, like he did, say, on 'Mood Indigo', or whatever. And other times, I mean -- or more times -- it wasn't that often that he came up with a big melody, but he was always coming up with music for the band.
Yeah. He always came up with music for the band.
Yeah.
But when his biggest hits and things -- was when he had the original band, when guys would chip in and help.
Yeah. Yeah. That's where all the big songs really came, out of that.
Yeah.
Didn't they?
Yeah. That's where all the big songs came from.
